request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: The Affordable Care Act was projected to reduce federal deficits overall, despite adding substantial gross spending for expanded coverage. A contemporaneous March 2010 estimate projected a $138 billion deficit reduction over 2010–2019 for the ACA and reconciliation changes together (CRS R41126, PDF p. 4). A later CBO/JCT estimate projected a $210 billion reduction over FY2012–FY2021, alongside $1,390 billion in gross coverage-expansion costs over the same period (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These were projections, not actual realized results, and use different periods and baselines. [Open the full brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-164321-4e7a.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified CRS findings answer the overall budget effect and clarify that net deficit estimates differ from gross coverage costs; estimates are projections and not comparable across periods/baselines.
